svg.title: Adversarial Filtering (HellaSwag/WinoGrande) and Prefix-Swap Suffix Scoring
svg.desc: Left panel illustrates the iterative Adversarial Filtering (AF) and AFLite pipeline where generator distractors that are easily detected by a discriminator ensemble are iteratively replaced until spurious lexical shortcuts vanish. Right panel illustrates WinoGrande's prefix-swap suffix scoring where the candidate entity replaces the blank in the prefix and the model scores only the identical post-blank suffix.
svg.text: Commonsense & Coreference Benchmarks: Adversarial Filtering & WinoGrande Scoring
How HellaSwag removes lexical artifacts and why WinoGrande scores the post-blank suffix instead of the pronoun
A. Adversarial Filtering (HellaSwag & WinoGrande)
Removing annotation artifacts that let context-free classifiers cheat
Step 1: Candidate Pool Generation (G_theta)
Sample N candidate wrong endings (ActivityNet / WikiHow) or
crowdsourced Winograd twin sentences around anchor words.
Step 2: Ensemble Discriminator Audit (D_phi / AFLite)
Train m linear/MLP classifiers on random train splits to predict
the gold label from shallow features or frozen embeddings phi(x, y).
Predictability score: s(i) = (1/m) sum_{j=1..m} P_j(gold | x_i)
Step 3: Prune High-Predictability Shortcut Items
Discard top-k easiest distractors/instances where s(i) > tau;
resample until discriminator accuracy drops toward chance.
Result: Smooth Pretraining Scaling Signal
• Trivial bag-of-words / unigram heuristics score ~25–30%.
• Base LLM accuracy climbs smoothly from 100M to 70B parameters.
B. WinoGrande Prefix-Swap Suffix Scoring
Sentence: "The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because _ was too big."
Wrong Method: Score Candidate Entity at the Blank "_"
Compare log P("trophy" | "... because") vs log P("suitcase" | ...)
Fatal flaw: The decisive word "big" (vs "small") comes AFTER "_"!
Both twin sentences have the exact same prefix before "_"!
Correct Method: Swap Candidate into Prefix, Score Shared Suffix
1. Form two conditioning prefixes by substituting e_1 and e_2:
Prefix 1: "... fit in the suitcase because the trophy"
Prefix 2: "... fit in the suitcase because the suitcase"
2. Score conditional log-prob of the IDENTICAL post-blank suffix:
s_1 = log P(" was too big." | Prefix 1) = -3.10 (Winner)
s_2 = log P(" was too big." | Prefix 2) = -5.85
Why Prefix-Swap Eliminates Both Length & Prior Bias:
Because the scored target string (" was too big.") is identical in both
passes, token length L and word frequency of e_1 vs e_2 never enter the sum!
